project_dependencies.use: PG755 AGN owns the neuter accusative plural sāptāni.
3.14 lexical ratna and t instruction already owned.
Canonical rule keys for numeral derivation, marker accents, repetition and the compound.

source_observations.observation: Joined verse with the measured groups, treasures, their recipient, distribution and praise.
Separates tris and ā, gives the distributive pair and segments the praise word.

source_observations.locator: Sāyaṇa on RV 1.20.7, textual and grammatical exposition
source_observations.observation: His singular group definition, concrete threefold ritual classification and five accent explanations have different functions.
The two annotators disagree on the cases of the syncretic neuters. Both identify the presser as dative and praise as instrumental.
The number can be attached to the wealth, the libations of the presser, or the additional rites, depending on the interpretation.
The opening and the line with three and seven identify a Ṛbhu recitation and a feature of the ninth day.
PG755 direct parallel under the verb of gratifying. The creation of offspring belongs to a following clause.
The grammatical creation wording has the seven groups as object. The modern exposition separately cites RV 1.20.7.

source_observations.locator: Pañcapādī digital row 3014, frozen source file
source_observations.observation: 3.14 gives ram, na and t. Sāyaṇa's printed numbering 3.294 identifies the same rule by wording.
The ñ or n marker can converge on the same position of accent.

source_observations.locator: 6.1.173, accent on the ending after the specified śatṛ stem
source_observations.observation: Sāyaṇa invokes this rule for the dative of the soma-presser.
The special rule for the ktin member takes precedence in the praise compound.
The distributive repetition designates the later item as āmreḍita, with its own accent consequence.
